input.sql: SELECT l.opp_id, l.similarity, o.account_id, a.name, o.opp_type, o.stage, o.status, o.amount_usd, o.loss_reason, substr(o.notes,1,160) notes FROM v_opp_links l JOIN crm_opportunities o USING(opp_id) JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=o.account_id WHERE l.theme_id='TH-04' ORDER BY o.amount_usd DESC

SELECT source, account_id, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT substr(body,1,60)) distinct_bodies, min(created_at), max(created_at) FROM v_feedback WHERE theme_id='TH-04' GROUP BY source, account_id ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 40

SELECT l.opp_id, l.similarity, o.account_id, a.name, o.opp_type, o.stage, o.status, o.amount_usd, o.loss_reason, substr(o.notes,1,160) notes FROM v_opp_links l JOIN crm_opportunities o USING(opp_id) LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=o.account_id WHERE l.theme_id='TH-02' ORDER BY o.amount_usd DESC
SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT body) distinct_bodies, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT source) srcs FROM v_feedback WHERE theme_id='TH-02' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 15
SELECT source, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) accts, COUNT(DISTINCT body) distinct_bodies, AVG(urgency) urg, SUM(mentions_workaround) wa FROM v_feedback WHERE theme_id='TH-01' GROUP BY source
SELECT body, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) accts, MIN(feedback_id) ex FROM v_feedback WHERE theme_id='TH-01' GROUP BY body ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT event_name, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) accts FROM telemetry_events WHERE feature_key='console_theme' GROUP BY event_name

SELECT l.opp_id, l.similarity, o.account_id, a.name, o.opp_type, o.stage, o.status, o.amount_usd, o.close_date, o.loss_reason, substr(o.notes,1,200) notes FROM v_opp_links l JOIN crm_opportunities o USING(opp_id) LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=o.account_id WHERE l.theme_id='TH-03' ORDER BY o.amount_usd DESC

SELECT source, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) accts, COUNT(DISTINCT body) distinct_bodies, MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT f.*, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id) cnt FROM v_feedback f WHERE theme_id='TH-03') GROUP BY source

SELECT f.account_id, a.name, a.is_customer, a.arr_usd, COUNT(*) n, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT f.source) srcs FROM v_feedback f LEFT JOIN accounts a USING(account_id) WHERE theme_id='TH-03' GROUP BY f.account_id ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 25

SELECT a.account_id, a.name, a.is_customer, a.arr_usd, a.renewal_date, a.csm_health, COUNT(*) n FROM v_feedback f LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=f.account_id WHERE f.theme_id='TH-01' GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY a.arr_usd DESC LIMIT 8
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_opp_links WHERE theme_id='TH-01'

SELECT c.item_id, c.account_id, a.name, a.arr_usd, a.renewal_date, c.speaker, c.kind, substr(c.text,1,140) text FROM v_cab_items c LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=c.account_id WHERE c.theme_id='TH-04' ORDER BY c.item_id
SELECT account_id, name, arr_usd, renewal_date, csm_health, is_customer FROM accounts WHERE name='Aspen Energy' OR account_id IN ('ACC-0232','ACC-0258','ACC-0360','ACC-0356')

SELECT o.opp_id, o.account_id, a.is_customer, a.arr_usd, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_feedback f WHERE f.account_id=o.account_id AND f.theme_id='TH-02') fb, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telemetry_events t WHERE t.feature_key='agent_policy_editor' AND t.account_id=o.account_id) ev FROM v_opp_links l JOIN crm_opportunities o USING(opp_id) JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=o.account_id WHERE l.theme_id='TH-02'

SELECT COUNT(*) total, COUNT(DISTINCT lower(trim(body))) distinct_bodies, COUNT(DISTINCT substr(lower(body),1,40)) distinct_prefix, SUM(account_id IS NULL) null_acct FROM v_feedback WHERE theme_id='TH-02'

SELECT f.feedback_id, f.account_id, f.body, (SELECT count(*) FROM telemetry_events t WHERE t.feature_key='scim_sync' AND t.account_id=f.account_id) scim_events, (SELECT count(*) FROM telemetry_events t WHERE t.feature_key='scim_sync' AND t.account_id='ACC-0372') delta_scim FROM v_feedback f WHERE f.theme_id='TH-04' AND f.account_id='ACC-0392'

SELECT t.account_id, SUM(event_name='task_started') st, SUM(event_name='task_abandoned') ab, ROUND(1.0*SUM(event_name='task_abandoned')/NULLIF(SUM(event_name='task_started'),0),3) rate, MIN(ts), MAX(ts) FROM telemetry_events t WHERE feature_key='approval_flow' AND account_id IN ('ACC-0385','ACC-0397','ACC-0230','ACC-0337','ACC-0267','ACC-0223','ACC-0271','ACC-0010','ACC-0354','ACC-0311') GROUP BY t.account_id

SELECT feedback_id, source, account_id, created_at, substr(body,1,160) body FROM v_feedback WHERE theme_id='TH-03' AND (account_id IN ('ACC-0385','ACC-0397') OR account_id IS NULL) UNION ALL SELECT item_id, 'cab_item', account_id, meeting_id, substr(text,1,160) FROM v_cab_items WHERE theme_id='TH-03'

input.reason: Nearly all the feedback (86 of 93) comes from the idea portal, and most of it is short, templated "+1 for dark/night mode" posts (e.g. FB-00240, FB-00244, FB-00253, FB-00203) with an average urgency of about 1.6. Users drop tasks in console_theme at a normal rate (1,967 of 17,920 starts, about 11%, which is the same as non-complainers). No deals are linked to this theme, so the $378K "influenced" figure is just the combined ARR of accounts that posted, mostly one post each, led by Red Retail (ACC-0256). It's a real but low-stakes request that's nice to have, and the score should go down further.

checks.question: Is the feedback from one loud source, or duplicated/templated?
checks.finding: 86 of 93 mentions are from idea_portal and spread across 51 accounts. Many are near-identical '+1 dark/night mode' posts built from the same 'Would make late-night on-call nicer' phrase (FB-00240, FB-00244, FB-00253, FB-00229, FB-00256). Average urgency is 1.6, and only 18 mention a workaround.

checks.question: Do users actually struggle with the feature?
checks.finding: console_theme has 17,920 task starts and 1,967 abandons (about 11%) across 400 accounts. That matches the 10.8% rate for non-complainers, so there's no friction difference.

checks.question: Is there real revenue behind it?
checks.finding: v_opp_links has 0 deals for TH-01. The dollars-influenced figure is just the ARR of posting accounts, led by Red Retail ACC-0256 ($205K, 1 post) and Onyx Logistics ACC-0263 ($150K, 1 post). None of the posts tie the request to renewal risk.

input.reason: The theme holds up. The feedback is not templated: all 82 messages are distinct, and they come from many accounts and sources. The 11 linked deals are spread across 11 accounts and name this gap directly, and three of them (OPP-00542, OPP-00546, OPP-00549) were lost with it as the stated reason. One small caution: every deal has the same one-line note and a modest match score of about 0.52. Also, 7 of the 11 are prospects with no product usage, so the deal side partly depends on CRM text rather than seen behavior.

checks.question: Is the deal money concentrated in one account, or linked only by weak text matches?
checks.finding: The 11 deals ($88k–$281k each, about $2.08M total) are on 11 different accounts. None dominates; the largest is OPP-00550 at $281k. Every deal has the same note, 'Gap: agent permissions too coarse, security blocked rollout', and a match score of 0.52–0.53. That reads like a standard CRM gap tag, but it names the theme directly. input.reason: The usage pain looks real: 7 of the 9 complaining accounts use remote sessions, and they abandon tasks about twice as often as the rest of the user base (roughly 23% vs about 12%). The money case is thin, though. About 60% of the dollars come from Orbit Analytics (ACC-0399, $835K ARR, 5 of the 22 mentions), no deals are linked to this theme, and two cited accounts never use the feature: Red Studios (ACC-0275) and Granite Studios (ACC-0142), whose only mention is a side note in a dark-theme request (FB-00202). Much of the rest is repeat Zendesk tickets that use the same wording: 4 from Summit Networks (ACC-0151) and 4 from Cedar Retail (ACC-0245), plus 2 tickets with no account attached (FB-00396, FB-00407).

checks.question: Is the revenue/feedback concentrated in one account?
checks.finding: Orbit Analytics (ACC-0399, $835K ARR) accounts for 5 of 22 mentions and ~60% of dollars influenced; no other account exceeds $200K.

checks.question: Are any deals actually linked to this theme?
checks.finding: v_opp_links returns zero opportunities for TH-13; the pay pillar rests only on existing-customer ARR, not pipeline or lost deals.

checks.question: Do complainers actually use remote_session?
checks.finding: 7 of 9 accounts show telemetry. ACC-0275 (Red Studios) and ACC-0142 (Granite Studios) show none, and FB-00202 is an 'unrelated' aside in a dark-theme idea.

checks.question: Is the friction abnormal versus baseline?
checks.finding: Complainer abandonment rate is about 23% (e.g., ACC-0399 24/104, ACC-0325 16/66, ACC-0132 11/27). The baseline across all 88 accounts is 522/4469, about 11.7%. This supports a real issue.

checks.question: Is feedback duplicated or templated?
checks.finding: Summit Networks (FB-00403 to FB-00406) and Cedar Retail (FB-00408, FB-00409, FB-00411, FB-00412) filed near-identical Zendesk tickets that use the same phrasing. FB-00396 and FB-00407 have no account.

input.reason: All 19 mentions say the same thing, "Is there a Terraform provider?" (two even share the same typo pattern). Every one has urgency of 2–3, and none mention a workaround, a blocker or any business impact. That looks like a common pre-sales or FAQ question, not a product pain point. The $1.67M "pay" figure is just the combined ARR of the accounts that asked, mostly Quartz Systems, Blue Legal and Harbor Analytics: no deals are linked to this theme, and no opportunity notes, loss reasons or CAB items mention Terraform.

checks.question: Is the feedback real demand, or the same question repeated?
checks.finding: All 19 items are word-for-word 'Is there a Terraform provider?' (FB-00619 and FB-00588 have typos). Urgency is 2 everywhere except FB-01055 at 3, and none mention a workaround or impact. Two Gong items (FB-00588, FB-01377) have no account attached, and Iron Robotics (ACC-0177) appears twice.

checks.finding: v_opp_links returns no rows for TH-16.

checks.question: Does Terraform come up in CRM notes, loss reasons or CAB meetings?
checks.finding: No opportunity notes or loss reasons mention Terraform, and no CAB items are tagged TH-16 or mention it.

checks.question: Is the $1.67M influenced revenue tied to churn or renewal risk?
checks.finding: It is just the ARR of the accounts that asked, mostly ACC-0385 (Quartz Systems, $1.39M, health yellow), ACC-0394 (Blue Legal, $1.22M, green) and ACC-0395 (Harbor Analytics, $1.08M, green). None of the feedback links their renewals to Terraform.

input.reason: The complaint is real and comes from several accounts: five accounts (Fern Energy, Granite Capital, Atlas Media, Onyx Foods, Bright Bio) report the same OS-upgrade problem in Zendesk and at CAB, and two of those also raised it at CAB. But both Jira items attached to this theme (FB-00507, FB-00484) are about access policies, not patching. The complaining accounts add up to only about $0.7M ARR, while most of the $9M "influenced" figure comes from large green-health accounts like Aspen Insurance (ACC-0391), which never raised this issue and whose usage fell only slightly (42 to 36 task starts). There are also no linked deals, and complainers abandon patch tasks at almost the same rate as everyone else (12.3% vs 11.3%), so usage data doesn't show friction specific to this problem.

checks.question: Is the feedback from real, distinct accounts that actually belong to this theme?
checks.finding: Of 16 feedback rows, 13 Zendesk tickets match the theme and come from 5 accounts (one has no account). Fern Energy alone filed 4 near-identical tickets. Both Jira items (FB-00507 Aspen Retail, FB-00484 Silver Networks) are about access policies and were mis-clustered here.

checks.question: Does CAB evidence back it up?
checks.finding: Yes. There are 3 pain points and 2 asks from ACC-0237, ACC-0292 and ACC-0230, but only two speakers (Ravi Novak raised the ACC-0237 and ACC-0292 items).

checks.question: Is the dollar figure tied to the accounts that complain?
checks.finding: No. The top account, Aspen Insurance (ACC-0391, $1.4M ARR, green), has no feedback on this theme, and its patch usage fell only slightly (42 to 36 task starts). The complaining accounts total about $0.7M ARR, and the theme has no linked deals.

checks.question: Do complainers show abnormal friction with the feature?
checks.finding: Not clearly. Abandon rates vary by account (0% to 21%), and complainers average 12.3% vs 11.3% for others, so the usage data doesn't separate them.

input.reason: This is a request from one prospect, not a market need. Globex Holdings is not yet a customer, and one open deal (OPP-00539, $1.24M, still in evaluation) accounts for the whole revenue case. The "3 accounts" count is inflated: the Vantage Foods (FB-00147) and Lumen Labs (FB-00148) quotes repeat Globex's own wording and talk about Globex's requirement, not their own. FB-00170 is about Ubuntu enrollment and is unrelated. Those two customers' SAML setup abandon rates (12–14%) are about the same as everyone else's, and Globex itself shows no product usage, so there's no sign of wider pain.

checks.question: Who actually raised this, and is the feedback independent?
checks.finding: 8 of 12 items are tagged to Globex (ACC-9001, a prospect, is_customer=0) and 1 untagged item (FB-00142) is also from Globex. FB-00147 (Vantage Foods) and FB-00148 (Lumen Labs) repeat Globex's wording ('Globex won't sign without it', 'Globex procurement made it a hard requirement'). FB-00170 is about Ubuntu enrollment and is unrelated. All 12 items come from one source, Gong.

checks.question: Is the revenue spread across deals?
checks.finding: Only one deal is linked: OPP-00539, a Globex new-logo deal for $1.24M, open and in evaluation. The AE's note says custom SAML regex transforms are the only blocker. There is no expansion or renewal money at stake.

checks.question: Do the other tagged accounts show trouble with SAML setup in usage data?
checks.finding: In saml_config, ACC-0025 abandons 12% of started tasks and ACC-0171 abandons 13.8%. That is close to the 11.1% baseline. ACC-9001 has no saml_config events because it is a prospect.

input.sql: SELECT theme_id, title, feature_key, size FROM v_themes WHERE title LIKE '%agent%' OR problem_statement LIKE '%agent%'

SELECT a.account_id, a.name, a.arr_usd, a.renewal_date, a.csm_health, a.seats, COUNT(*) n, MIN(f.created_at), MAX(f.created_at)
FROM v_feedback f JOIN accounts a USING(account_id)
WHERE f.theme_id='TH-02' AND f.source='gong' AND a.segment='Mid-Market' AND a.is_customer=1 AND f.created_at >= date('2026-11-26','-60 days')
GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY a.arr_usd DESC

SELECT account_id,
 SUM(event_name='task_started') st, SUM(event_name='task_completed') co, SUM(event_name='task_abandoned') ab,
 COUNT(DISTINCT user_hash) users, COUNT(DISTINCT substr(ts,1,10)) active_days,
 COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ts>=date('2026-11-26','-30 days') THEN user_hash END) users_30d,
 MIN(ts), MAX(ts)
FROM telemetry_events WHERE feature_key='agent_policy_editor' AND account_id IN ('ACC-0234','ACC-0347','ACC-0286','ACC-0348','ACC-0305','ACC-0239')
GROUP BY account_id

SELECT a.segment, a.is_customer, COUNT(DISTINCT f.account_id) FROM v_feedback f JOIN accounts a USING(account_id) WHERE f.theme_id='TH-02' AND f.source='gong' AND f.created_at >= date('2026-11-26','-60 days') GROUP BY 1,2

SELECT feedback_id, account_id, created_at, urgency, mentions_workaround, body FROM v_feedback WHERE theme_id='TH-02' AND source='gong' AND account_id IN ('ACC-0348','ACC-0305') AND created_at>=date('2026-11-26','-60 days')

input.answer:
Six mid-market customers raised AI agent permissions (theme TH-02, "Can't scope AI agent permissions") on Gong calls since 2026-09-27. Together they renew **$573,200 ARR**, all between May and October 2027:

| Account | ARR | Renewal | CSM health | Agent policy editor usage: started / completed / abandoned | Users (all time / last 30d) | Active days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vantage Studios | $228,400 | 2027-10-25 | green | 45 / 30 / 15 | 24 / 6 | 39 |
| Cedar Logistics | $90,300 | 2027-08-07 | green | **no usage recorded** | – | – |
| Fern Retail | $83,100 | 2027-05-03 | yellow | 77 / 44 / 33 | 29 / 14 | 58 |
| Fern Energy | $81,600 | 2027-07-08 | green | 94 / 57 / 37 | 28 / 15 | 69 |
| Delta Insurance | $46,400 | 2027-07-11 | green | 47 / 30 / 17 | 26 / 8 | 39 |
| Atlas Health | $43,400 | 2027-10-25 | red | 37 / 19 / 18 | 22 / 6 | 33 |

**Usage isn't sticky.** Activity data runs from about 2026-05-31 to late November 2026. Only about 51–67% of started tasks get completed, so roughly a third to half are abandoned. Only 6–15 people per account used the editor in the last 30 days, against 582–2,439 seats.

**Customers are working around the tool, not using it.**
- Cedar Logistics, with no recorded use, says permissions "can't be limited to a group or OU" and it "blocks the expansion" [FB-00060].
- Vantage Studios and Atlas Health "spun up a separate tenant just to sandbox agent identities" [FB-00055][FB-00068].
- Fern Energy says the editor "times out" and they "gave it a throwaway account and hope for the best" [FB-00083].
- At Fern Retail, legal has blocked it "until it's fixed" [FB-00050].
- At Delta Insurance, the audit flagged unrestricted copilot directory access [FB-00045].

**Most at risk:** Fern Retail has the earliest renewal (May 2027) and yellow health. Atlas Health is rated red. Vantage Studios is the largest contract ($228,400).

SELECT a.segment, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT f.account_id) accts, SUM(f.mentions_workaround) wa, ROUND(AVG(f.sentiment),2) sent FROM v_feedback f JOIN accounts a USING(account_id) WHERE f.theme_id='TH-05' GROUP BY a.segment

SELECT a.name, a.arr_usd, a.renewal_date, a.csm_health, COUNT(*) n FROM v_feedback f JOIN accounts a USING(account_id) WHERE f.theme_id='TH-05' AND a.segment='Enterprise' GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY n DESC

SELECT q_score,b_score,evidence_score,archetype,priority_rank,json_extract(metrics,'$.top_share') ts, json_extract(metrics,'$.top_account') ta, skeptic_notes FROM v_theme_scores WHERE theme_id='TH-05'

content.text:
Enterprise customers are unhappy because they **can't preview or test which users a conditional access change will lock out** (theme TH-05). Two caveats first: the enterprise evidence is small and mostly from one account, and most of this complaint actually comes from Mid-Market customers.

**What enterprise customers say:**
- **Bad changes have locked people out.** Cobalt Robotics locked out its CEO by accident [FB-00515] and had a sev-2 incident from a bad rule [FB-00513].
- **They avoid tightening policies.** "Changing conditional access is a leap of faith with 4,000 users. We avoid tightening policies at all" [FB-00514].
- **They use costly workarounds.** One keeps a spare "break-glass" admin account just in case [FB-00516]. Another tries every change on a single pilot group for a week first [FB-00521]. 6 of the 8 enterprise items mention a workaround like this.
- **They all ask for the same fix:** a dry-run, what-if or policy-simulator mode [FB-00514, FB-00521, CAB-M04-L22, FB-00513].

**How big it is:**
- **Enterprise is a small slice.** It's 8 items from 4 accounts, and Cobalt Robotics wrote 5 of them. Mid-Market has 29 items from 12 accounts, with similar negative sentiment (−0.61 vs −0.57 for enterprise).
- **The enterprise accounts aren't flagged at risk.** All 4 (Cobalt, Iron Freight, Pine Robotics, North Media) are rated green health, with renewals in 2027. The nearest is Cobalt on 2027-01-04, and an account rep there asked whether this was "a blocker for the renewal" [FB-00513].
- **Across all segments, the problem is real.** The theme ranks #7 in priority and was raised by 4 different accounts in customer advisory board meetings. Usage data shows complaining accounts abandon 32% of conditional access tasks, versus 11% for other accounts. One $110k expansion deal was lost over this exact gap.

input.sql:
SELECT r.item_id, r.title, r.status, r.target_quarter, g.theme_id, t.title AS theme, g.similarity, json_extract(s.metrics,'$.top_share') AS top_share, json_extract(s.metrics,'$.top_account') AS top_account, t.size, s.priority_rank
FROM roadmap_items r JOIN v_gpl_links g ON g.item_id=r.item_id JOIN v_themes t ON t.theme_id=g.theme_id LEFT JOIN v_theme_scores s ON s.theme_id=g.theme_id
WHERE r.status IN ('committed','in_build') ORDER BY top_share DESC

SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts WHERE is_customer=1 AND renewal_date BETWEEN '2026-11-26' AND date('2026-11-26','+150 days')) n_renew, (SELECT SUM(arr_usd) FROM accounts WHERE is_customer=1 AND renewal_date BETWEEN '2026-11-26' AND date('2026-11-26','+150 days')) arr, (SELECT group_concat(feature_key) FROM features) feats, (SELECT MIN(ts)||' '||MAX(ts) FROM telemetry_events WHERE feature_key=(SELECT feature_key FROM features LIMIT 1)) rng

WITH r AS (SELECT account_id FROM accounts WHERE is_customer=1 AND renewal_date BETWEEN '2026-11-26' AND date('2026-11-26','+150 days'))
SELECT t.feature_key,
 SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-09-25' AND event_name='task_started' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) recent,
 SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-07-27' AND ts<'2026-09-25' AND event_name='task_started' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) prior,
 COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ts>='2026-09-25' THEN t.account_id END) acc_recent,
 COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ts>='2026-07-27' AND ts<'2026-09-25' THEN t.account_id END) acc_prior,
 ROUND(1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-09-25' AND event_name='task_completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-09-25' AND event_name='task_started' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) compl_recent,
 ROUND(1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-07-27' AND ts<'2026-09-25' AND event_name='task_completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-07-27' AND ts<'2026-09-25' AND event_name='task_started' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) compl_prior
FROM telemetry_events t JOIN r ON r.account_id=t.account_id
WHERE t.feature_key IN ('agent_policy_editor','approval_flow','browser_ext','bulk_import','conditional_access','console_theme','device_inventory','device_trust','linux_enroll','patch_policies','remote_session','saml_config','scim_sync','user_lifecycle') AND ts>='2026-07-27'
GROUP BY t.feature_key ORDER BY 1.0*recent/NULLIF(prior,0)

WITH r AS (SELECT account_id,name,segment,arr_usd,renewal_date,csm_health FROM accounts WHERE is_customer=1 AND renewal_date BETWEEN '2026-11-26' AND date('2026-11-26','+150 days')),
x AS (SELECT r.account_id,name,segment,arr_usd,renewal_date,csm_health,
 SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-09-25' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) recent,
 SUM(CASE WHEN ts<'2026-09-25' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) prior
 FROM telemetry_events t JOIN r ON r.account_id=t.account_id
 WHERE feature_key='patch_policies' AND event_name='task_started' AND ts>='2026-07-27' GROUP BY r.account_id)
SELECT segment, COUNT(*) n, SUM(recent) recent, SUM(prior) prior, SUM(CASE WHEN recent<0.7*prior THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_down30, SUM(CASE WHEN recent<0.7*prior THEN arr_usd ELSE 0 END) arr_down30 FROM x GROUP BY segment

SELECT substr(ts,1,7) m, COUNT(*) FROM telemetry_events t JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE feature_key='patch_policies' AND event_name='task_started' AND a.is_customer=1 AND a.renewal_date BETWEEN '2026-11-26' AND date('2026-11-26','+150 days') GROUP BY m ORDER BY m

WITH r AS (SELECT account_id,name,segment,arr_usd,renewal_date,csm_health FROM accounts WHERE is_customer=1 AND renewal_date BETWEEN '2026-11-26' AND date('2026-11-26','+150 days'))
SELECT r.name,segment,arr_usd,renewal_date,csm_health,
 SUM(CASE WHEN ts>='2026-09-25' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) recent,
 SUM(CASE WHEN ts<'2026-09-25' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) prior
 FROM telemetry_events t JOIN r ON r.account_id=t.account_id
 WHERE feature_key='patch_policies' AND event_name='task_started' AND ts>='2026-07-27' GROUP BY r.account_id HAVING recent<0.7*prior ORDER BY arr_usd DESC LIMIT 8

input.query: patch policies not working, stopped using patching, rollout problems

content.text:
I looked at the 150 customer accounts that renew between now and 2027-04-25, which together hold $18.58M in ARR. Of the 14 features, only **patch policies** shows a real drop in usage.

- **How much:** Tasks started in patch policies fell from 1,045 (7/27–9/24) to 777 (9/25 to now), about 26% lower. The same 64 accounts are still using it, so they're using it less rather than abandoning it, and the completion rate barely moved (0.90 → 0.87). By month, usage peaked at 602 in August, then fell to 454 in September and 426 in October. November has 266 so far, but the data ends 11/23, so that month is incomplete.
- **Who:** The drop is concentrated in larger accounts. Enterprise usage fell from 362 to 229, and 8 of 11 Enterprise accounts dropped more than 30%, covering $5.75M ARR. Mid-Market fell from 451 to 315, with 13 of 23 accounts down more than 30% ($1.31M ARR). SMB was flat (232 → 233).
- **Accounts to watch:** Aspen Insurance ($1.40M, renews 2/20, 28 → 19), Blue Legal ($1.22M, 3/14, 41 → 19), Red Bio ($847K, 1/12, yellow, 38 → 18), Birch Insurance, Onyx Retail, Silver Freight (red health, renews 1/9) and Harbor Insurance (yellow, renews 12/19, the soonest). Most of these are rated green by their account managers despite the drop, so health scores may be missing the risk.
- **Likely reason:** Customers report that patch policies stop applying after OS upgrades (macOS 16, Sequoia point releases, Windows 11 feature updates). They often only find out from vulnerability scans or auditors, and some have moved patching to another tool [FB-00156][CAB-M05-L20][FB-00160][CAB-M03-L20]. Deferral settings are also being ignored [FB-00157]. These complaints come from Mid-Market accounts that aren't necessarily on the renewal list, so the link to the drop is an inference, not proven.
- **Everything else** is flat or up. The agent policy editor grew from 351 to 477, though only 15 of the renewing accounts use it.

The comparison is between two roughly 60-day windows of "task started" events.

- **Accounts to watch:** Aspen Insurance ($1.40M, renews 2/20, 28 → 19), Blue Legal ($1.22M, 3/14, 41 → 19), Red Bio ($847K, 1/12, yellow, 38 → 18), Birch Insurance, Onyx Retail, Silver Freight (red health, renews 1/9) and Harbor Insurance (yellow, renews 12/19, the soonest). Most of these are rated green by their account managers despite the drop, so health scores may be missing the risk.
- **Likely reason:** Customers report that patch policies stop applying after OS upgrades (macOS 16, Sequoia point releases, Windows 11 feature updates). They often only find out from vulnerability scans or auditors, and some have moved patching to another tool [FB-00156][CAB-M05-L20][FB-00160][CAB-M03-L20]. Deferral settings are also being ignored [FB-00157]. These complaints come from Mid-Market accounts that aren't necessarily on the renewal list, so the link to the drop is an inference, not proven.
- **Everything else** is flat or up. The agent policy editor grew from 351 to 477, though only 15 of the renewing accounts use it.

The comparison is between two roughly 60-day windows of "task started" events.
